sixtySeconds.whatItDoes: VoiceStudio is a desktop AI voice app that runs on your own device. It can clone voices, design new voices from a description, dub videos into other languages, transcribe, dictate and narrate audiobooks.
sixtySeconds.problem: Most AI voice tools are cloud services that charge per minute and need your audio uploaded. VoiceStudio runs the models locally, so you choose the engines, download only what you need and keep your recordings on your machine.
whoFor: Creators narrating videos, stories or audiobooks
People dubbing videos into other languages
Writers and developers who want local dictation and transcription
Developers automating voice work through an API or MCP
sixtySeconds.whyChoose: Choose it if you want a free, local voice studio with many engines in one app. Check each model's license: the default OmniVoice weights are non-commercial.
requirements: macOS 13.3+ on Apple Silicon, Windows 10/11 x64, or Linux x64
An NVIDIA GPU helps (AMD ROCm on Windows is opt-in); CPU works too
Disk space for the voice models you download

overview: VoiceStudio bundles voice cloning from a clean reference recording, video dubbing with speech timed to the original, voice design from a text description, a floating dictation widget, local transcription, and narration with queued batch jobs. The README says it covers 646 languages.

It starts with the VoiceStudio engine (powered by k2-fsa/OmniVoice) and lets you pick other engines in its Model Manager, downloading only the models you need. A local API, MCP server, reusable recipes and watch folders let you automate it.

The app is free under AGPL-3.0 and needs no account. VoiceStudio Pro is an optional paid closed-source build with a commercial license for client work across several machines, and VoiceStudio Cloud is a hosted API that isn't available yet. Neither license covers model weights.

steps.code:
brew tap debpalash/tap
brew trust --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio
brew install --cask debpalash/tap/voicestudio
